T-002.Title: Make the omitted-boundary C6 call a content witness, and keep explicit-boundary and active-mode git checks

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: windowsEvidenceProblems of this repository with the boundary argument omitted returns an empty list, spawns no git process, and still returns empty when the injected git runner would fail every call. The six archive sha256 pairs and the twelve paths are the pins in the spec. One changed byte, one extra file, or one missing pinned file fails closed and restoring it greens the call. The green result does not contain the absent-boundary sentence or the not-an-ancestor-of-HEAD sentence. candidateSha must equal b7c94d786ebc89cc279c6dc292c8dd32110fcc9d.

An explicit boundary keeps git ancestry, the historical diff, the archive-byte diff, and the existing allow and emptiness rules. A passed boundary that is absent or not an ancestor of that repository HEAD fails closed. Omitting the boundary on a throwaway whose archive bytes do not match the six pins fails closed, and passing that throwaway its own boundary still greens the git path. Active mode does not consult the content pins. The object-aware git diff helper is not called by the omitted path. When either object is absent it reports a named reason. The fixture discovery test plants a .test.ts under the fixture directory, sees artifactIsStale true, and sees false again after the file is removed. No new .test.ts file is added under src/ or scripts/.

T-003.Title: Upload the exact-head Ubuntu JUnit artifact from the validate job and add the portable verifier

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The validate job stays on ubuntu-latest. Its first checkout keeps fetch-depth 0 and is not retargeted. Later steps check out the pull-request head sha, or the pushed sha, with fetch-depth 0, install, run the two pre-pin files with -t b53d13d and the JUnit reporter, write prepin-behavior-head.txt, and upload both files with actions/upload-artifact@v7 as prepin-behavior-junit, including after a failed test step. A missing file fails the upload. The job does not run ngrace gate verdict and does not commit run-ledger.xml.

scripts/verify-prepin-linux-evidence.ts is the one bun:test file the CloseEvidence command runs. Its name does not contain .test. It takes no local-report argument and no environment switch. It selects the newest gh run for git rev-parse HEAD on validate.yml, requires status completed and conclusion success, checks the head stamp, and accepts the report only when each of the two titles is exactly one testcase with no skipped, failure, or error child. Other skipped testcases are ignored. A missing run, a failed run, a head mismatch, a missing title, or a forbidden child fails the test. The task command is bun test --timeout=0 scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts -t "prepin linux verifier". It executes this file through a gh binary on PATH and refuses a newest failure that has an older success, a missing run, a wrong or missing head stamp, a missing, duplicate, skipped, failed, or error target, a missing gh binary, and a failed download. It also reads the workflow and simulates the step graph locally: the upload still runs after a failed control, and a missing junit or head file fails the job. That simulation is not a GitHub Actions execution. A file that only contains the pinned words passes a string check and fails this command. The CloseEvidence command is expected non-zero until the authority has pushed the closing commit and the Ubuntu job for that sha has succeeded. The executor does not invent that run.
